title: I built a free 2D game engine you make with your own coding agent, then customize by hand
author: BlazeEcho
selftext:
Been building this for a while and it's finally not embarrassing enough to post. It's a completely free (no subscription, no up-charge) 2D game engine called Hearth, and the whole idea is you build the game by talking to whatever coding agent you already use, Claude Code or Codex or whatever you've got. So it runs on the agent you're already paying for, no extra subscription or API key stacked on top.

I built it because I wanted something where the agent does the building but I still get a normal editor underneath, so the moment I want to change something I just open it and do it by hand like any other engine instead of re-prompting the model four times to nudge one platform. That loop drove me insane in every other setup I tried.

Other reason I didn't just point an agent at Godot and call it a day is that here the agent can actually run the game and check it works before it tells you it's done, so you're less likely to get something that looks finished and then falls apart the second you hit play.

It's free, runs locally, your project is just files on your machine. It's early and not perfect in places so  I'd really appreciate people just messing with it and tell me what's rough. Point your agent at it and try to build something. 

https://reddit.com/link/1v1zod2/video/6rrdpxglkgeh1/player

Feedback in this thread, or at [hearthengine.com/feedback](http://hearthengine.com/feedback) would be greatly appreciated!

Link: [hearthengine.com](https://hearthengine.com).

comments.author: Interesting-Yam23
comments.body:
\> Other reason I didn't just point an agent at Godot and call it a day is that here the agent can actually run the game and check it works before it tells you it's done

  
You can just add a few lines to your [agents.md](http://agents.md) with some rules about how to invoke godot, read scenes, dump scene output, and write scripts for piloting tests with screenshots or whatever. Works perfectly. Not sure what the use is in having it embedded directly.

replies.author: BlazeEcho
replies.body:
yeah you can rig that up, but that's kind of the thing. you're scripting the piloting and screenshot stuff yourself and babysitting it, and IMO it gets flaky fast. here it just works out of the box and stays reliable cause the engine's actually built for it.

honestly though this was more a passion project than trying to beat a giant like godot. big engines are gonna be better at tons of stuff, no question. i just wanted my own take on one that's ai native from the ground up instead of bolting an agent onto something that was never built for it. still figuring out new ways and updates to make it fit claude code better than engines that never had agents in mind.

replies.author: Interesting-Yam23
replies.body:
\> you're scripting the piloting and screenshot stuff yourself and babysitting it

I don't think you need to babysit it much? Write the tools, point the agent at it and let it rip. My screenshot/scene dump/annotation tools haven't needed much work. Agents kind of just get it.

And I totally get the hobby project, great job on that front. I guess I just find Godot already \*really\* agent friendly for everything I'm trying to do, the workflow of having agents and the editor open simultaneously already works.

I'm also really interested in learning/testing how to make agents behave better in dev, if you're able to get great results with your engine, specifically with a \*mature\* game project (not one-shot stuff), I'd be super interested to see your results.

replies.author: Asaroz
replies.body:
I have just told opus it can test its changes with the godot cli and it can run games with head or headless, controll it, measure performance of individual methods.  
A lot of stuff that godot is offering itself.   
Your project is cool i like it but it cant solve a problem i do not have.

replies.author: BlazeEcho
replies.body:
Jaja, sí, Godot la primera vez es un caos. Ojalá esto te sirva más. Pruébalo mañana y dime qué te parece. Está temprano, así que cualquier cosa rara me ayuda. ¡Gracias, me alegra que te gustara el video!

\*translated, I do not speak Spanish

comments.author: moreauver
comments.body: I uilt something similar recently that I'll be showing off soon, I'll give yours a look!

comments.author: Turbulent-Leather-77
comments.body: I made a 2D game engine completely cordless and with almost every feature a creator would need. I ended up scrapping it. I love the idea, and maybe it can truly benefit someone, but with the way AI is heading (and it’s coming very soon), I don’t see a practical need for community engines anymore unless it’s huge a huge company with a custom engine that has real techs on site. It’s a lovely idea, but in my opinion, claude will be able to write a game better than any mainline engine enthusiast could do, and after all… claude made it. Best of wishes.

replies.author: BlazeEcho
replies.body: thanks for sharing your experience! I see what you mean and I'll reconsider my approach

replies.author: Turbulent-Leather-77
replies.body: You’re welcome. I hope you gather success off your engine. Don’t give up!
